value.author: samMularczyk
value.layerInfo: Redraw the image as a grid of text characters.

textSize: Size of one character cell in pixels.
cellAspect: Cell height as a multiple of its width. Above one gives tall cells, like real monospaced type.
margin: Padding inside each cell, as a fraction of it. Higher values space the characters further apart.
charset: Which glyph ramp to use. Classic is pixi.js's eight-level dot-to-hash ramp; Block Density, Dots, and Numeric are five, eight, and eleven steps native to this plugin; Letters and Full ASCII are twenty-six and ninety-five steps from the Tom Thumb font.
rampGamma: Bias of brightness onto the glyph ramp. Below one favours dense glyphs, above one sparse.
rampContrast: Pushes cells toward the sparsest and densest ends of the character set. A character set is a short ladder - Classic has eight rungs - so midtones crowd into the middle of it and the extreme glyphs hardly get used. This spends the whole set, which is the punchy posterised look that reads as ASCII art. Ramp Gamma cannot do it: gamma moves the midpoint but leaves both ends pinned.
structure: Picks the glyph whose SHAPE matches the cell rather than just its brightness, so an edge becomes a slash or a bar running the same way. Only available for Letters and Full ASCII: the other sets are density ramps of symmetric marks - Classic's eight glyphs are all but one symmetric - so there is no directional glyph for this to find and it correctly does nothing. Candidates stay near the density the cell already has, so tone survives; higher widens that search.
edgeThreshold: Above zero, cells on a boundary use a line glyph chosen by edge direction. This is the threshold the edge must clear.
colorMode: Colour from the layer, one flat colour with transparency between glyphs, or ink on a filled paper.
inkColor: Character colour, used by Single Colour and Ink On Paper.
paperColor: Background colour, used by Ink On Paper.
paletteLevels: Quantises each cell's colour to this many steps per channel. Zero is off.
invert: Flip the brightness ramp, so dark areas get the dense characters.
randomChars: Chance of a cell using a random glyph instead of its brightness one, for a scattered letterform look.
seed: Changes which cells are scattered and which characters they get.
amount: Mix between the original layer and the character result.
